The spine of the developmental trauma work here

NARM therapy

NARM, the NeuroAffective Relational Model, is a therapy for developmental trauma: the patterns laid down early, before you had words or choices, that still shape how you meet your own life. It starts from curiosity rather than diagnosis, and it works with what the past installed rather than excavating the past itself. Reem Glasco, LPC-S, is a NARM therapist, and NARM is the spine of most of her work with developmental trauma. Sessions are 50 minutes at $240 self-pay, online anywhere in Texas, with Blue Cross Blue Shield accepted.

What NARM actually does

Every child adapts to the environment they are given. If closeness was unsafe, you learned distance. If your needs made things worse, you learned not to have them. If being competent earned the only reliable attention going, you learned to be useful. Those are not flaws. They are solutions that worked, and they kept working long after the conditions that required them had gone.

NARM calls these adaptive survival styles, and its interest is not in cataloguing them but in what they cost you today. The invitation is to notice how a pattern keeps you from being present in your own life, and to discover through felt sense which direction leads toward thriving rather than toward more of the same.

This is why NARM is less about the story than most therapies. The history matters, but understanding your history is famously compatible with nothing changing. What shifts things is working with the pattern as it shows up in the room, in the present tense.

It tends to fit when

  • The trouble is a lifelong pattern rather than a single event.
  • You understand your history intellectually and nothing has changed.
  • Self-criticism is doing most of the talking.
  • You disconnect from what you want before you have finished wanting it.
  • Other people's needs arrive clearly and your own arrive late or not at all.

How a NARM session feels

Slower than you expect, and more curious than sympathetic. The question is rarely what happened and more often what is happening right now as you say it: what your attention does, where it goes instead, what arrives in your body when you name something you want.

Agency is the quiet subject throughout. Developmental trauma teaches people that their own impulses are dangerous or irrelevant, and NARM keeps returning the choice to you, including the choice to not go there today.

What it is not

It is not catharsis, and it does not ask you to relive anything. It is also not advice. If you want a therapist who will tell you what to do about your mother, this is the wrong model and worth saying so early.

Questions about NARM

What is NARM therapy?

NARM is the NeuroAffective Relational Model, a therapy developed by Dr Laurence Heller for developmental trauma. It works with the adaptive survival patterns formed early in life and with how they shape the present, rather than with the events themselves. Its organizing question is where a pattern was learned, how it was serving you, and whether it still is.

What does NARM stand for?

The NeuroAffective Relational Model. Neuro for the nervous system, affective for emotion, relational because the patterns it works with formed in relationships and show up in them.

How is NARM different from regular talk therapy?

Conventional talk therapy tends to build an account of what happened. NARM is interested in what is happening now: how you relate to what you are saying, where your attention goes instead, and what your body does when you name something you want. Insight is a side effect rather than the goal.

Is NARM the same as somatic therapy?

No, though they overlap and are often used together. Somatic therapy works primarily through bodily sensation. NARM works with identity, agency and the adaptive patterns that organize them, using felt sense as one source of information among several.

How long does NARM therapy take?

Longer than single-incident work, because the target is capacity rather than a symptom. Patterns built over a childhood do not unwind in six sessions. The arc is reviewed together as the work goes rather than promised at the start.

Can I do NARM therapy online?

Yes, and it is the default here. NARM tracks your attention, your relationship to what you are saying and your felt sense, none of which require being in the same room. Both you and your therapist must be physically located in Texas during a session, because that is where this practice is licensed.

This practice does not provide emergency care. If you are in immediate danger, call 911. For a mental health crisis, call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
